newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty still below resistance, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty still below resistance, seen rising.

text.p: The zloty refrained from attacking strong resistance levels at 2.5 percent from parity on Monday as volatile dollar/mark swings took centre stage despite large-scale foreign entry into Polish T-bills.

"Dollar/mark moves ruled the market today with currency selling pressure sometimes felt, but resistance levels remained closely watched and were not crossed," Maciej Grabosz, forex dealer at Bank Zachodni SA.
Dealers said the zloty's resistance levels could be tested on Tuesday and Wednesday as foreign investors paid for an estimated 150 million zlotys worth of T-bills on Monday.
The zloty closed at 2.52/2.47 percent from the trading band centre, just down from Friday's 2.54/2.51 percent.
It closed at 3.1400/20 to the dollar, down from 3.1445/55 on Friday and at 1.8552/57 to the mark, up from 1.8495/00.

At the tender minimum prices all fell but average yields for the 26-week and 52-week remained pitted around 21.40 percent. The average yield for the shortest 13-week paper fell to 20.82 percent from 21.00 under pressure from corporate bids.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates eased slightly to close at 22.45/22.65 and 22.50/22.80 percent in light trade.
